grammar.label: remote conditions — were to, should, happen to
grammar.form: If + subject + were to + base verb; Should + subject + base verb
grammar.meaning: marks a condition as unlikely or purely hypothetical

explanation.en: 'If the rate were to double' is more remote than 'if the rate doubled'; 'Should the rate double' is the formal inverted version. 'If you happen to see her' marks the condition as chance rather than plan.
explanation.uz: 'If the rate were to double' — 'if the rate doubled' dan ko'ra uzoqroq ehtimol. 'Should the rate double' — rasmiy inversiyali varianti.

grammar.positive_example: Were the rate to double, the scheme would close.
grammar.negative_example: Were the rate would double, the scheme would close.

l1_notes.uz: Shart darajalari o'zbek tilida ohang bilan beriladi; ingliz tilida esa qurilma tanlovi bilan.

grammar.label: negative purpose — lest, for fear that, in case
grammar.form: lest + base verb / should; for fear that + clause; in case + clause
grammar.meaning: states what an action is meant to prevent

explanation.en: 'He said nothing, lest he make it worse' gives the thing avoided, not the thing sought. 'Lest' takes the base form and is already negative, so no 'not' follows. 'For fear that' and 'in case' do the same work in plainer registers.
explanation.uz: 'lest' oldini olinayotgan narsani bildiradi, o'zi inkor ma'noli, shuning uchun keyin 'not' qo'yilmaydi va fe'lning asosiy shakli keladi.

grammar.positive_example: She kept a copy, lest the original be lost.
grammar.negative_example: She kept a copy, lest the original will not be lost.

l1_notes.uz: 'lest' juda kitobiy; og'zaki nutqda 'in case' yoki 'so that … not' ishlatiladi.

body.text: Were the bridge to close, how would the school open on Monday?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Should it close, what happens on Monday?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Then we would take the children round by the east road.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Write it down, lest we work it out in the dark and the rain.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: He is right about this one. Every plan has a shortcoming. Name it before the weather does.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: The east road floods as well.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then the plan has two limitations, not one. Write both.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: An earlier start, or a boat from the farm. Neither is expensive.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: There is no incentive to plan for a bridge that stands.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: None at all, until the morning it does not. I keep the page short in case somebody has to read it fast.
